hook.h2: He spoke first, and He used her name
hook.text: "Hagar, Sarai's servant," he said, "where have you come from, and where are you going?" "I'm running away from my mistress Sarai," she replied.
father: "where have you come from, and where are you going?"
hook.note: Hagar was a servant, pregnant, running, and nobody's first concern. Our Father found her at a spring in the wilderness, opened with her name, and asked her a question instead of passing a verdict. She is the first person in Scripture to give Him a name of her own — the One who sees me — and she gave it after being heard. That is the exchange this edition is built for: His words in BLUE on the page, and two inches of blank margin beside them for yours.

short350: You have wanted a Father your whole life. Not a doctrine about Him. Not a distant power. A Father — His voice, His heart turned toward you.

Father's Heart Bible is the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking: our Father's words in BLUE, the Son's in RED, the Spirit's in PURPLE. For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 128,579 words across 5,615 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies.

She Hears Her Father's Voice is the journaling edition, written to her. The complete Bible — 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses, not abridged — in 8 x 10 full color, single column, with an outside margin over two inches wide on every page for her notes, prayers, and answers to Him. The color marks ownership, not quotation: His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.

When our Father found Hagar in the wilderness, she was running, pregnant, and unwanted. He spoke first and called her by name, and she named Him the One who sees me. An introduction opens each book, and a Father's note closes each with a short prayer. The opening pages — Abba Father, She Hears Her Father's Voice, a message from Kevin and Shelly, Receiving Your Father, the Preface and About this Translation — speak to her as His beloved daughter. A presentation page carries her name.
He is not distant. He is not disappointed. He is your Heavenly Father, and He delights in you as His beloved daughter.
A fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek. A gift, a keepsake, an heirloom.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

body: Father's Heart Bible™ (FHB): She Hears Her Father's Voice Journaling Bible. A complete wide margin journaling Bible for women, 8 x 10, in full color — the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's words in RED. The Spirit's words in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, the red letter Bible has shown you the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 128,579 words across 5,615 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. He has been speaking the whole time. No Bible has ever shown you where.

When our Father found Hagar in the wilderness, she was running, pregnant, and unwanted. He spoke first, and He called her by name. She heard Him, and she named Him: the One who sees me (Genesis 16:13). This Bible was made to show you where He has already spoken to you.

God is our Father. Not a role He plays. Father is who He is, and Father is His name, the name Jesus came to reveal: "I revealed your name to those you gave me from the world" (John 17:6). You are His beloved daughter, and He delights in you.

If the word father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you. The Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood. He is the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.
Complete Bible — 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses. Not abridged.

faq.q: How wide are the margins, and can I actually write in them?
faq.a: Two inches of blank, unruled paper beside every page of Scripture — enough for a dated note, a prayer, or a few lines of your own beside the verse they belong to. That is what the larger 8 x 10 page buys: the text stays readable in two columns and the margin stays genuinely usable, instead of the narrow strip you get when a 6 x 9 tries to be a journaling Bible.

faq.q: How is this different from the other fifteen editions?
faq.a: It is the only one that is not 6 x 9. This is an 8 x 10 hardcover of 848 pages, laid out in two columns with a two-inch writing margin, and it is $124.99 rather than $99.99 because of the larger trim and page. The translation inside is the same complete Father's Heart Bible™ in Divine Voice Color — 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses — and the opening pages are written for a woman.

faq.q: Why is it called She Hears Her Father's Voice?
faq.a: Because of Hagar. She was a servant, pregnant and running, and our Father came to her at a spring in the wilderness, spoke first, and asked her a question rather than passing a verdict. She is the first person in Scripture to give Him a name of her own — the One who sees me. The edition is named for what happened to her, and built so it can happen on your page.

It is made to be one. There is a presentation page for her name, a giver and a date, and a wide-margin Bible is one of the few gifts that gets more personal every year it is used. Order direct and shipping is free.

For a hundred and twenty-five years red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 128,579 words across 5,615 verses — and until now those words were printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. In Divine Voice Color you see who is speaking: our Father's words in BLUE, the Son's in RED, the Spirit's in PURPLE. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation — His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored.

faq.q: Can I read it online as well?
faq.a: Yes, free, in twenty-five languages, at fathersheartbible.com/read — with English and Telugu also free to listen to. The print edition is the one with the margin to write in.
